title: Technical English — Course 4, Semester 1 — Pilot Variant 3

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When will the component workshop begin?
tasks.audioText: The electronics department will hold a component identification workshop on Monday at nine forty-five. Students should bring the illustrated component chart from the course folder. The instructor will compare resistors, capacitors, diodes and transistors, focusing on their symbols and general functions. The workshop will use photographs and unpowered training boards.

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. Which chart should students bring?
tasks.audioText: The electronics department will hold a component identification workshop on Monday at nine forty-five. Students should bring the illustrated component chart from the course folder. The instructor will compare resistors, capacitors, diodes and transistors, focusing on their symbols and general functions. The workshop will use photographs and unpowered training boards.

tasks.prompt: A capacitor stores electrical energy in an electric field and can be used in several types of electronic circuit. A diode is designed to conduct mainly in one direction, while a transistor can be used for switching or amplification. Component appearance alone is not enough for identification; the printed code, circuit symbol and component documentation should also be checked. Reading 1. What can a capacitor do?
options: Store electrical energy in an electric field

tasks.prompt: Why is appearance alone insufficient for identification?
options: Because the printed code, symbol and documentation should also be checked

tasks.prompt: A diode is designed ___ mainly in one direction.
Choose TWO components commonly used in electronic circuits.
A semiconductor component that can be used for switching or amplification is a ___.
You cannot identify a component from its appearance. What should you do?
options: Choose the component that looks closest.
Check its printed code and compare it with the component documentation.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of electronic components in a logical order.
options: Compare the code and symbol with the reference
Observe the component and its label
correctOrder: Observe the component and its label
Compare the code and symbol with the reference

tasks.prompt: Write 80–100 words describing the general functions of a capacitor, diode and transistor. Explain why component identification should use documentation.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: task completion and relevant content (0–2); clear organisation and logical linking (0–2); grammar and sentence structure (0–2); accurate electrical vocabulary, spelling and punctuation (0–2). Minor errors are acceptable if meaning remains clear.
